title: Rotation Sequence
author: Nelyn
rules:
Rotation Sequence

+

THE RULES

Normal Sudoku

Normal Sudoku rules apply.

Positive Diagonal

The digits cannot repeat on the positive diagonal.

Concentric Rings Rotation

The grid is divided into four concentric square rings, labelled A (outermost) to D (innermost).

Each number in the sequence rotates its indicated ring and all rings outside it.

The number gives the distance moved in cells along each affected ring's perimeter:
→ clockwise, ← counterclockwise.

The centre cell remains fixed.

FINAL ROTATION

After applying the entire sequence, the four rings must form one coherent rotation of the original grid, meaning either 0°, 90°, 180°, or 270°.

The digits to put in the grid are the ones before the rotation !

Both the original and resulting grids must satisfy all Sudoku rules and all constraints, even the clues between the grid and the sequence above the grid.

The sequence must be filled with the digits 1 to 9 exactly once each.

Region Sum Lockout Lines

Each purple line follows both rules:

Region Sum: The digits on each segment of the line, separated by 3×3 box boundaries, must have the same sum (counting diamond ends).

Lockout: The digits in the two endpoint diamonds must differ by at least 4. Digits along the line cannot have values strictly between the two endpoint digits.

Kropki Dots

Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive.

Arrow

Digits on an arrow line sum to the digit in the bulb attached.
